about.title: About VERA-DAR
about.opening: **VERA: Verifiable Evidence-based Research Answers**, an agentic research system for provenance-grounded evidence evaluation and auditable synthesis.
opening_expansions: **-DAR: Domain-Aware Retrieval**: VERA-DAR adds domain-aware retrieval to VERA.
**-MAGOPS: Multi-Agent Operations**: VERA-DAR-MAGOPS is a proposed multi-agent operations control plane for VERA-DAR (planned; not part of this service).
about.intro: This page explains what VERA-DAR is and how it answers. Other pages show a one-line notice that links here.

after_disclosure.heading: News reports
paragraphs: For questions about current events, VERA-DAR may use news reports found through the GDELT news index. It reads a report only from outlets on its allowlist and only where the site's robots rules and terms permit; reports from other outlets are shown as links only.

corpus_page.title: Corpus Description
paragraphs: This page describes VERA-DAR's collection of stored sources. It first gives the number of sources and the date of the newest source.

It then shows the subject areas the collection covers, with each area's share of the documents and its main topics and subtopics. The subject areas, topics and subtopics come from VERA-DAR's subject list. Each document is listed once, under the closest subject on that list. No language model is used, so this part is shown even when no written description is available. Documents that match no listed subject are counted as not matched. The matching is approximate, so treat the shares as a rough guide.

When a checked description is available, the page also shows a short description of the collection, its main topics with each topic's share of a sample of the sources, and its current coverage. That description was written by a language model. The page says so, gives the date it was written, and the description may be imperfect. When no checked description is available, the page shows the publication years instead.
The page never names an individual source.

how_to_use.title: How to use VERA-DAR
how_to_use.intro: A short guide to asking a question and reading what comes back.

sections.heading: What to ask
paragraphs: Type one research question in your own words on the Ask VERA-DAR page, then press Enter.

For the best answers, ask about subjects already in VERA-DAR's collection. VERA-DAR answers from documents it has already collected, so questions on those subjects get the most complete answers. Other questions can still work, but VERA-DAR first has to find and read new sources, so they are slower and less likely to get an answer.

VERA-DAR does not write or fix code; it can point to published research instead. A question outside the collection may get a reading list instead of an answer. Some requests are refused for safety reasons.
sections.corpus_link: See what the collection covers on the Corpus Description page

sections.heading: What you get back
paragraphs: An answer, marked Answer, cites the documents it is written from with numbers such as [1]. {answer_sources} An answer marked Partial answer does not cover every part of the question.

Evidence and limitations lists the limits of the answer and a short quoted excerpt for each cited number, with whether the claim was supported or partly supported. Research and verification holds the process notes and the claim check.

When VERA-DAR cannot answer from its documents it says so and shows a reading list: documents that may be relevant, with links, that VERA-DAR has not read. Declining to answer is a valid outcome, not an error; read the listed documents yourself.

sections.heading: How to read the citations
paragraphs: A number in the answer matches the same number in the cited passages under Evidence and limitations and in the source list. Where no excerpt is shown, the line says so and gives the passage reference instead.

Under Research and verification, the Evidence scope line says how many stored documents have passages matching the key terms of your question (or that none was relevant) and how many passages were selected as possible evidence. The Claim check line says how many cited claims a model checked against the passages, and how many were supported, partly supported or removed.
Where a licence requires it, an attribution line names the creator, title and licence of the cited document.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: The checks are automated, not human review, and can be wrong. Quotes are short excerpts, not whole documents. Open the sources and read them before relying on a claim.
Requests are rate-limited; if you reach the limit, wait and try again later.
If the service has been idle it may need up to about {wake_minutes} minutes to start; your question is kept while it starts.

sections.heading: The other pages
paragraphs: Report: either a live report from asking VERA-DAR, or an offline example labelled "illustrative, not a real run".
Trace Eval: a dated evaluation run (Historical) and, once collection is switched on, live usage statistics (Live). The Historical figures describe that earlier run, not the current service.

sections.heading: Terms and privacy
paragraphs: The Terms of Access, Browsing, and Use page says what VERA-DAR keeps from your question, for how long, which outside AI and search services receive it, and the terms for using VERA-DAR.

terms.intro: These terms apply when you access, browse or use VERA-DAR, including its API. By using VERA-DAR you agree to them; if you do not agree, please do not use it. This page also holds VERA-DAR's privacy notice.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: **What VERA-DAR collects.** VERA-DAR has no accounts and does not ask who you are. It receives the question you type, and keeps a record of the steps taken to answer it (which services were used, timings, outcome), with nothing that identifies you. Please do not put names, contact details, health information, ID or account numbers, or other personal details in a question.

**Why.** To answer your question, and to diagnose errors. Where EU or UK data protection law applies, the legal basis is the operator's legitimate interest in running and fixing this free educational service.

**Who receives it.** To answer, your question, or search terms taken from it, is sent to AI model providers and to the search and data services listed above under Third-party sources and licences, and, for current-events questions, to the GDELT news index. The AI model providers include Groq and, only as a fallback, OpenAI. If the free providers run out while an answer is being written, your question, the passages found and the draft answer may be sent to OpenAI to finish that answer. VERA-DAR uses hosting by Render in the United States; Render reports that it is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (we have not checked this against the official list). These services are in the United States, except Europe PMC (United Kingdom), and have their own data-handling and retention policies.

**How long.** How long VERA-DAR keeps your question is set out under "Your question and what is stored" below. By default Groq does not retain inference data, but it may keep abuse-monitoring logs for up to 30 days unless Zero Data Retention is on. OpenAI, used only as a fallback, may keep abuse-monitoring logs for up to 30 days. This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice. VERA-DAR uses your IP address only briefly, in memory, to apply request limits, and does not store it; the hosting provider may record IP addresses in its own logs for security and operation.

**Your rights.** You can ask what VERA-DAR holds about a question you sent, or object to its use. VERA-DAR has no accounts and no email contact, so raise a request by opening an issue titled "Privacy request" on {repo_issues}. Issues are public: do not put your question text, your name or any other personal details in the issue; the operator will reply there with how to identify the question privately. Stored questions are kept for up to 30 days; VERA-DAR cannot yet delete a single question earlier on request. If you are in the EU or the UK you may also complain to your data protection authority.

**Sale and tracking.** VERA-DAR does not sell or share personal information, shows no advertising, uses no analytics and does not track you across sites. It does not respond to Do Not Track signals because it does no tracking.

**Children.** VERA-DAR is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect their information. If you believe a child has sent personal information, open a "Privacy request" issue as described above, without including that information.

sections.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: VERA-DAR sets one cookie, `_streamlit_xsrf`, which protects your session against cross-site request forgery. It is strictly necessary, so no consent is needed. Your browser also keeps the sidebar width, whether the sidebar is open and the colour theme on your device; this stays on your device. VERA-DAR uses no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
